divergences.old: openshift resource-usage --csv printing raw CSV to stdout instead of the envelope
divergences.toil: --csv writes the CSV to a file in the workspace named with --out <file>, never overwriting, and data is the JSON result with the saved absolute path added as file. Nothing but the envelope goes to stdout
divergences.why: Every command writes exactly one envelope; CSV goes to a file only (decision 4 on #68).

divergences.toil: --out <file> is added, and --csv requires it (and --out requires --csv), checked before any request
divergences.why: Where the CSV goes has to be named, since it no longer goes to stdout (decision 4 on #68).

divergences.old: Named clusters as openshift.environments.<env>.instances.<instance>.{baseUrl, token} beside flat openshift.baseUrl and openshift.token, with openshift.defaultEnvironment and openshift.defaultInstance picking one; --env or a default environment with no instance (or the reverse) failed, naming the missing flag
divergences.toil: Each cluster is an openshift connection, with env and instance settings for a named one. --env and --instance each select the connection named <name>, or the one whose env (or instance) setting is <name>, and must agree when both are given; either alone is enough when it identifies one connection, and a value that matches several is INVALID_INPUT naming them. defaults.openshift.connection takes the place of defaultEnvironment and defaultInstance. An unknown name is INVALID_INPUT listing the clusters toil knows
divergences.why: toil's config is a set of named connections, and --env is the one environment concept that selects among them (decision 9 on #68), so clusters can't be a nested map inside one connection.

divergences.old: With openshift.defaultEnvironment and openshift.defaultInstance set, the stored cluster's baseUrl and token won over the OPENSHIFT_BASE_URL and OPENSHIFT_TOKEN env vars, which only set the flat cluster (#88 item 3)
divergences.toil: TOIL_OPENSHIFT_* env vars configure the default connection and win over anything stored for it. Another connection takes only its own TOIL_CONN_<NAME>_* variables, then defaults.openshift; the TOIL_OPENSHIFT_* token never fills a gap in it
divergences.why: Env vars outrank every stored value, and a credential goes only to the connection it's configured on.

divergences.old: openshift cluster list reading every named and flat cluster from config with no connection, succeeding with count 0 when none was configured, and reporting openshift.defaultEnvironment and openshift.defaultInstance as stored
divergences.toil: It reports the one connection the call resolves (--env, --instance, --connection or the default), with a meta.warnings entry saying so and pointing at toil connections list for every connection. Each cluster gains its connection name. With no openshift connection it fails NOT_CONFIGURED, and with several and no default INVALID_INPUT. defaultEnvironment and defaultInstance are the connection's env and instance when the call used the default connection, otherwise null
divergences.why: An area command sees only the connection its call resolved, never the config, so no area can read another connection's settings (CLAUDE.md, Commands never read config or env). Listing every connection is toil connections list's job.

divergences.old: openshift logs failing at once on HTTP 429, with no retry
divergences.toil: A 429 is retried as on every other request (honouring Retry-After up to 30 s, three attempts) before failing with HTTP
divergences.why: Every request goes through core's one HTTP layer, which retries a 429 the same way for every command.
